title: DO NOT WORSHIP THE CREATED THINGS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: or like any creature that moves along the ground or any fish in the waters below. And when you look up to the sky and see the sun, the moon and the stars—all the heavenly array—do not be enticed into bowing down to them and worshiping things the Lord your God has apportioned to all the nations under heaven. But as for you, the Lord took you and brought you out of the iron-smelting furnace, out of Egypt, to be the people of his inheritance, as you are now. - Deut 4:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses continues the warning, now addressing the temptation to worship the sun, moon, and stars. Ancient peoples often worshiped the heavenly bodies as gods. But Moses reminds Israel that these are created things God has "apportioned to all the nations" — they are God's handiwork, not deities to be worshiped. To bow to the sun or stars would be to worship the creation instead of the Creator.

There is a beautiful contrast in these verses. Instead of worshiping created things, Israel was to remember what the Creator had done for them: "the Lord took you and brought you out of the iron-smelting furnace, out of Egypt." God had rescued them from the crushing furnace of slavery to make them "the people of his inheritance." The God who made the sun and stars had personally redeemed them. Why would they trade this living, redeeming God for lifeless created things?

This exposes the folly of all idolatry. It bows to what is made rather than to the Maker; it serves the gift rather than the Giver. But the true God is not only the Creator of all things — He is the Redeemer who reaches down to rescue His people. He is worthy of all worship.

For us, the same truth stands. We are surrounded by good things God has made, and we are tempted to worship them — to make ultimate what God intended as gifts. But we are called to worship the Creator, who has done something even greater than the exodus for us. Through Christ, He has brought us out of the furnace of sin and made us His own treasured possession (1 Pet 2:9). Let us worship the Redeemer, not the created things, giving our hearts to the God who made us and saved us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you tempted to worship God's good gifts rather than God Himself?
2. How does remembering God's redemption guard you against idolatry?
3. How has God brought you out of the "furnace" of sin through Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Creator and Redeemer, You made all things and rescued me from the furnace of sin through Christ. Help me to worship You, the Giver, and never the gifts, giving my whole heart to You alone. Amen.
